statement: Replacing the RMSNorm and adjacent elementwise sequence with a single fused kernel raises num_steps and lowers val_bpb in the frozen 300s H200 v2c scope, by removing redundant round trips to HBM.
rationale: RMSNorm is 18.6% of GPU kernel time over 10,653 launches and other elementwise Triton work is a further 8.1% over 32,071 launches, together 26.7% of kernel time for operations that move memory rather than do arithmetic. At d_model 512 these are bandwidth-bound, so fusing the norm with its neighbouring scale/add/cast removes whole HBM traversals. This competes with the CUDA-graph hypothesis on purpose: one attributes the loss to gaps between kernels and the other to the kernels themselves, and they predict different diagnostics.

prediction.statement: Candidate val_bpb is below its frozen same-GPU control by more than the gate, with num_steps higher and the post-run profile showing a reduced RMSNorm kernel-time share.

falsifiers: The paired delta does not clear the gate.
num_steps does not rise, indicating torch.compile had already captured this fusion and the share was not recoverable.
A post-intervention profile shows the RMSNorm share unchanged, refuting the memory-traffic mediator regardless of the metric.
val_bpb changes at matched step count, which would mean the fused kernel is not numerically equivalent and the arm is invalid rather than informative.

intervention.summary: In train.py, fuse the RMSNorm with its adjacent cast/scale/add operations into one Triton kernel (or a single torch op the inductor will fuse), keeping the arithmetic numerically equivalent in float32 accumulation. Verify equality of the forward output against the current implementation before staging.
